correctness.rationale: The proof correctly normalizes each proper facet normal by projecting 1_I into H_0={sum u_i=0}, giving nu_I=sqrt(|I|(m-|I|)/m). Summing shifted inequalities over every disjoint tree frontier proves the upper bound. The inclusion-tree recursion M_I=max(z_I+rho nu_I,sum_child M_J) and a root-to-leaf mass allocation prove feasibility at the minimum; all optimal centers are exactly the shifted-facet polyhedron. Positive weights and connected root imply all asserted facets; no infinite argument relies on enumeration. Independently solving a Chebyshev LP in two nontrivial laminar examples agrees with the frontier quotients.
